## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the width cap and `Text.Wrap` do bound `PanelToolTip`, and the binding reasoning in the description holds. The control's `implicitWidth` comes from the text's unwrapped width (`Text.implicitWidth` is the natural line width regardless of the assigned width), so `Math.min(implicitWidth, maximumWidth)` does not feed back into itself. Tooltips narrower than the cap keep their width and layout, `Text.PlainText` is unchanged, and explicit newlines still break lines.

Two issues remain: the bar tooltip path described as the motivating case is not covered, and capped tooltips are no longer centred on their target.

### Bar widget tooltips do not go through `PanelToolTip`

The description says `tooltipText` flows through `WidgetButton` into this component. In the source, `WidgetButton` hands the text to the bar, which draws it in its own popup window:

```text
Bar widgets, custom modules, third-party plugins (bar.showTooltip)
  WidgetButton.onEntered            shell/Ui/WidgetButton.qml:102-105
    bar.showTooltip(root, tooltipText)
      tooltipWindow (PopupWindow)   shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml:1286-1347
        tooltipBubble               implicitWidth: tooltipLabel.implicitWidth + 20
          tooltipLabel: Text        no wrapMode, no width limit   <- unchanged

Panel tooltips (PanelActionButton, direct uses in panels)
  PanelToolTip                      shell/Ui/PanelToolTip.qml     <- capped + wrapped by this PR
```

`shell/Ui/Button.qml:130-150` also has its own inline `ToolTip` with an unbounded `Text`, which this PR does not touch.

**Impact:** a long `tooltipText` on a bar widget, including the right-anchored third-party widget case in the description, still renders as one unbounded line. Only panel tooltips gain the cap.

**Suggested change:** apply the same bound to the bar tooltip, for example `width: Math.min(implicitWidth, cap)` and `wrapMode: Text.Wrap` on `tooltipLabel`, with `tooltipBubble` sized from `tooltipLabel.width`. Alternatively, narrow the description and the new code comment to panel tooltips.

### Capped tooltips shift away from their target

`PanelToolTip` does not set `x`, so it inherits the Qt Quick Controls style binding (Fusion, Basic and Material `ToolTip.qml`):

```qml
x: parent ? (parent.width - implicitWidth) / 2 : 0
```

After this PR, `implicitWidth` stays at the unwrapped width while the actual width is the cap:

```text
target width b, natural width W, cap C (W > C)

before:  x = (b - W) / 2,  width = W   -> centred on target
after:   x = (b - W) / 2,  width = C   -> centre moves left by (W - C) / 2
```

Qt's popup positioner only moves the tooltip when it crosses a window edge, so away from edges the offset is not corrected.

**Impact:** the offset grows with text length, which is the case this PR targets. A tooltip with a 385px natural width moves about 32px left. At 1600px it moves 640px, far enough that the bubble no longer overlaps the item it describes.

**Suggested change:** centre on the actual width in `PanelToolTip`:

```qml
x: parent ? Math.round((parent.width - width) / 2) : 0
```

`width` depends only on `implicitWidth` and `maximumWidth`, so this adds no binding cycle. It was not runtime tested.

**Documentation note:** the description says tooltips shorter than the cap are unaffected, so there is no visual change for existing first-party widgets. At default theme values (11px monospace, about 298px of text width inside the 320px cap), two Agents panel tooltips in `shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml` can exceed the cap with ordinary usage values. These are the model-row usage tooltip (for example `In 1.0K · out 2.0K · cache read 3.0K · cache write 4.0K`, about 385px) and today's day-row tooltip when prompt stats are shown. These would now wrap and shift as described above. The widths are estimates from nominal font metrics, not measurements.

---

**Test scope:** source review of head `0ff8061` against its merge-base and the current `quattro` tip (`PanelToolTip.qml` and the callers above are unchanged between them), plus upstream Qt qtdeclarative 6.8.3, 6.10.2 and 6.11.2 ToolTip, Popup, Control and Text sources and Quickshell 0.3.1. No runtime, rendering or on-screen measurement was performed. Pixel values are derived from source formulas and default theme tokens.
